clips.text: Welcome to Science Island! I am your Golden Frog explorer. Together, we will observe plants, follow the evidence, and discover how living things grow. Let your curiosity lead the way.
Look closely at a plant. Which part takes in water from the soil?
Roots take in water and minerals. Stems support the plant and carry water. Leaves use light to make food.
Observe the two leaves. Compare their shapes before you classify them.
We can observe leaf shape and color. We need to touch real leaves to compare how they feel.
Follow a bean flower. Pollen helps the plant make seeds. What develops around the seeds?
After pollination and fertilization, a bean flower can develop into a pod. The pod is a fruit that protects the seeds.
Put the stages of a bean plant in order, starting with a seed.
A bean seed can germinate, grow into a seedling, and become a mature plant. It can then make flowers, fruits, and new seeds.
Move the light. Observe how the young shoot changes its direction.
Many young shoots grow toward light. Roots usually grow downward in response to gravity. This diagram is a model, not a real time experiment.
Use what you have discovered. Read the evidence and explain your choices.
A good scientist observes carefully, compares evidence, and explains a conclusion. Keep asking questions!
